settings.cardStyleChromeNote: Anodised metal that takes each card's own colour - rose for Liked, blue steel for All songs - with a slow specular sweep across the plate.
settings.cardStyleMosaicNote: The collection's own sleeves, blurred into a soft field of its real colours rather than laid out sharp. It changes as your library does; a thin library simply shows fewer colours.
settings.cardStyleRichNote: The printed halftone, run on properly coloured stock instead of tinted paper. Pale paper is what made the old printed look go chalky: ink multiplied onto it cannot add colour the paper does not have. This drops the ground and darkens the ink to match, so the colour arrives without touching the dots.
settings.cardStyleStatNote: The count is the card, set large, with the object dropped to a watermark behind it. The doors that are really a number - Liked, All songs - lead with it. The look the app ships with.

settings.djVoiceHint: The DJ speaks its lines between songs - short cached clips from the server, ducked under the music. Needs a voice on the server (an ElevenLabs key, or the local model from install-voice.sh). This switch is per device.
settings.handbookAnatomyIntro: A directory under <c>{{dir}}</c>: a <c>{{manifest}}</c> naming it, and an entry module exporting one factory.
settings.handbookAnatomyPublic: <c>{{flag}}</c> is what puts a build into the official catalogue; without it the plugin still builds, for repositories you host yourself.
settings.handbookBooksFactAdd: Add a book puts one you own on the shelf. A phone cannot hand over a folder of chapters, so zip it and add the zip - the hub unpacks it and shelves the book, chapters intact.
settings.handbookBooksFactSkip: Where the transcript can see the publisher’s card and the closing credits, the book’s menu offers to skip both, remembered for that book alone.
settings.handbookBooksFactSpeed: Speed runs 0.75× to 2× without touching pitch - chapters, bookmarks and the words all stay exactly where they were.
settings.handbookBooksFactSpoken: Spoken words are searchable: half a remembered line surfaces as “Heard in your library” and plays from the moment it is said.
settings.handbookBooksReader: Playing one turns Now Playing into a reader. The hub transcribes a book ahead of time - the shelf’s Read along button asks, and a book’s hold menu can always ask for a fresh reading - and the words follow the narration word by word. Tap a line to play from its top; hold one to keep it, and the passage joins that book’s bookmarks carrying the sentence itself, kept with your account so a place marked on the sofa is there on the bus. Chapters get truthful names and a line each without spoilers, written by the hub’s AI - a preamble mislabelled Chapter 1 gets called a preamble.
settings.handbookBooksShelf: Audiobooks keep a shelf of their own, with a seat on the bar - a nightly book is a daily destination, and a twelve-hour reading loose in shuffle would be wrong every place it turned up. Books file under their authors, the hero’s one verb is Resume, and a transcribed book’s card says how fast its narrator actually reads - 168 wpm, brisk - the number that settles 1.25× before the book starts rather than ten minutes in.
settings.handbookBoothIntro: Behind the Booth sits a curator that reads the library - tempo, mood, what plays next to what - and builds mixes from what it learns. It counts a song as yours only when you finish it or heart it. A skip is not a listen, and the engine knows the difference.
settings.handbookBoothKnobs: Its knobs live in the Booth itself rather than in Settings: they are the taste engine’s own, opened from its room, not a pane about an abstraction.
settings.handbookBoothTitle: The Booth and the taste engine
settings.handbookBuildFactVersion: Bump the version before republishing - an installed bundle updates only when the version moves.
settings.handbookBuildIntro: One script builds every plugin into publishable bundles plus the repository manifest the marketplace reads. Each entry compiles to a single file whose host imports became table lookups; nothing from the app is bundled twice.
settings.handbookColophonHostRuntime: <c>{{path}}</c> - the module table a remote bundle builds against.
settings.handbookColophonIntro: The code is the reference, and it is written to be read.
settings.handbookColophonOutro: This handbook lives here in Settings, keeps your page, and is a plugin-sized feature itself - most of what it describes, it uses.
settings.handbookColophonRepo: <c>{{path}}</c> - working examples, from a preset rack to a whole importer.
settings.handbookColophonTypes: <c>{{path}}</c> - the whole contract, with the reasons in the comments.
settings.handbookConnectGroove: A groove is its own room, not a hand-off: the host’s player sets the pace, everyone else follows it, and in a friend’s groove a tap on any song sends it to their queue instead of yours - it shows as pending until their player picks it up. If the host steps out, the clock passes to whoever has been there longest.
settings.handbookConnectSeat: Every signed-in device appears in one registry, and exactly one of them holds the seat - the device actually making sound. The others are remotes: they see the same queue and drive the same playback, and pressing play somewhere claims the seat first, deliberately, so music never jumps rooms by accident.
settings.handbookCoverIntro: How the app works, and how to build for it - one page at a time. The first chapters walk the app the way a listener meets it; the last one is written at developers and ends with a plugin you could publish.
settings.handbookCoverTurning: Turn pages with the arrows below, the ← → keys, or a sideways swipe on the page itself. The bar above tracks where you are - tap a segment to jump to that chapter - and the counter between the arrows opens the whole index, every page of every chapter, from anywhere.
settings.handbookDeckFactEffects: Effects are rendered by the server, so a preset sounds identical on every device.
settings.handbookDeckFactQueue: The queue survives navigation - pages come and go, the deck does not.
settings.handbookDeckIntro: One queue, whatever feeds it - an album, a playlist, a station, a friend’s groove. Crossfade, the equalizer and the sleep timer live in Playback settings; the disc itself scratches under your finger, on a real tape loop, because a jog wheel that ignores physics is just a button.
settings.handbookDesignFactCascade: The app’s own stylesheet is a book of ordered chapters; order is the cascade, and a rule’s chapter is part of its meaning.
settings.handbookDesignFactKit: Plugins get the same kit and the same icons, so nothing they draw looks foreign.
settings.handbookDesignIntro: Every control comes from Glacier, the house component kit - buttons, fields, modals, the settings surface this handbook sits in - themed by tokens, so five themes and a rack of accents are data, not forks.
settings.handbookHostTableAvailable: Available: <c>{{react}}</c>, <c>{{kit}}</c>, <c>{{icons}}</c>, and the curated <c>{{seam}}</c> seam - the library, playlists, the session, the equalizer, platform truths.
settings.handbookHostTableFactContract: The table is a contract: adding is free, removing breaks every published plugin - so it only grows.
settings.handbookHostTableIntro: A repository plugin is compiled elsewhere but cannot bring its own React - a second copy could not share hooks with the app’s. So its imports compile down to lookups in a table the app installs on the global before any bundle runs.
settings.handbookIdentityFactAccount: One central account, whatever server you listen from.
settings.handbookIdentityFactJoin: Join a server with an invite, sign into one directly, or skip and stay local.
settings.handbookIdentityFactSkip: Skipped onboarding is never nagged about - joining later lives on the Friends page.
settings.handbookIdentityIntro: An account is who you are; a server is only where some music happens to live. So a fresh phone asks for the account first, and everything else hangs off it: the servers it can reach, the devices it plays on, the friends who can hear what you are into.
settings.handbookLibraryFactImports: Imports run on the server too - a phone can start one and put its screen to sleep.
settings.handbookLibraryFactPlaylists: Playlists live on the server when signed in, so every device sees one set.
settings.handbookLibraryIntro: Signed into a server, the server is the library - the phone, the desktop and the web all read the same shelves. A desktop with a local music folder feeds the hub rather than competing with it: it first asks the server what is missing, then sends only that.
settings.handbookNavFactBack: Drag in from the left edge to go back - the page follows your thumb, and letting go early puts it back.
settings.handbookNavFactPluginTabs: Plugins can add whole tabs here; the bar folds them in beside Home and Library.
settings.handbookNavFactSearch: Pull down on any page (or press ⌘K) to summon search over whatever you were doing.
settings.handbookNavIntro: The phone keeps its tabs on the bottom bar, the desktop keeps them on a rail - same items, the shape each platform holds naturally. Every page you open joins one back/forward history, so the app never loses your place.
settings.handbookOfflineFactPins: Pinned songs are sacred: never evicted, never counted against the cache budget.
settings.handbookOfflineFactSpace: Downloads & space shows both halves - how many songs are down here, and what they cost.
settings.handbookOfflineIntro: The phone keeps a self-rotating cache of what you actually play, ranked by how hot a song runs - recency and count together - so the plane test passes without anyone managing storage.
settings.handbookPairingFactWhere: Settings → Link a device on the signed-in side; the camera on the new one.
settings.handbookPairingIntro: Nobody should type a password on a phone keyboard. A device that is already in shows a one-time code - scan it and the new device is signed in, server address and all. The typed code underneath exists for the day the camera does not.
settings.handbookPluginChromeIntro: The chrome offers fixed mount points, and a plugin fills the ones it wants. A page is the biggest: a first-class navigation destination with its own nav item, walked by the app’s history like Home is.
settings.handbookPluginChromePages: <c>{{field}}</c> - label, icon, and a Content component handed <c>{{play}}</c> and <c>{{artist}}</c>; everything else it reads from context like a core page.
settings.handbookPluginChromeSections: <c>{{field}}</c> - tabs appended to this very modal, rendered behind the crash fence.
settings.handbookPluginDataDownloads: <c>{{field}}</c> - hand your queue to the Downloads page. Four states (queued, downloading, done, error), an optional <c>{{stage}}</c> for finer words, optional <c>{{parts}}</c> for the disclosure list.
settings.handbookPluginDataFactOneQueue: Never render your own queue page - a user watching two things arrive should not need to know which plugin owns which.
settings.handbookPluginDataIntro: Some contributions are data, not components, so the app keeps its own look and the plugin says only what the thing IS.
settings.handbookPluginDataTiles: <c>{{field}}</c> - a hook returning name, cover, tracks; the showcase draws the tile and wires play-through itself.
settings.handbookPluginHooksFactIds: Ids need only be unique within your plugin - the runtime namespaces them before merging.
settings.handbookPluginHooksFactOrder: Contributions render in registration order; nothing sorts, everything walks the array.
settings.handbookPluginHooksIntro: Plugin hooks run inside the runtime’s hook scope, which means the ordinary React rule matters doubly: call your own hooks unconditionally, in fixed order, before any early return. A hook that sometimes calls two hooks and sometimes three takes down its whole plugin.
settings.handbookPluginObjectIntro: No base class, no lifecycle methods, no manifest ceremony at runtime. A plugin is an object with an id, a name, and whichever contribution fields it wants to fill. Mounting and unmounting its contributions IS the lifecycle - React already owns that.
settings.handbookPluginObjectStable: Every field must be stable for the life of the app. Dynamism lives inside the components and hooks a plugin hands over, never in the shape of the object itself.
settings.handbookPluginObjectTitle: A plugin is a plain object
settings.handbookPluginPlatformsDesktopOnly: <c>{{flag}}</c> - shells out or walks the filesystem; never listed on a phone.
settings.handbookPluginPlatformsIntro: Three flags describe what a plugin needs, and the marketplace filters live against the platform and the session - a card offering something the device cannot do is worse than no card.
settings.handbookPluginPlatformsRequiresServer: <c>{{flag}}</c> - its whole value lives on the hub; absent everywhere until a server connects.
settings.handbookPluginPlatformsServerBacked: <c>{{flag}}</c> - a local engine will do (desktop), or a server will (anywhere); the importer reaches a phone the moment it signs in.
settings.handbookPluginProviderFence: Every contribution renders behind a fence: a throw anywhere pulls the whole plugin for the session - tabs, buttons, provider and all - and the app carries on. The Plugins pane says what left and why, rather than the app going down with a guest’s error.
settings.handbookPluginProviderIntro: A plugin’s <c>{{field}}</c> mounts around the app content, inside the core providers, so it may read the library and the session. Background work - queues, subscriptions, polling - lives here as ordinary effects, and switching the plugin off unmounts them all.
settings.handbookPluginProviderTitle: The Provider and the crash fence
settings.handbookPluginTwoWaysFactChannel: A repository is a distribution channel, not a dependency: removing a source uninstalls nothing.
settings.handbookPluginTwoWaysFactInstall: Installing downloads the bundle once and persists it - plugins load at boot, network or not.
settings.handbookPluginTwoWaysIntro: A plugin either compiles into the app - one line in the registry array, ordered in version control - or installs from a repository at runtime. A repository is just a URL serving <c>{{manifest}}</c> and one bundle file per plugin; the official one is baked in, and a server can host its own.
settings.handbookPluginVerbsAcquire: <c>{{hook}}</c> - ways to “get this” for a track, album or playlist. Say what you <c>{{can}}</c>; when several plugins can, the user chooses, and when none can, the Add control stays inert.
settings.handbookPluginVerbsCommands: <c>{{hook}}</c> - commands for the current search query. Mark one <c>{{flag}}</c> when the query is an action, like a pasted link, and songs should stand aside.
settings.handbookPluginVerbsIntro: Two hooks let a plugin answer the app’s questions in the moment they are asked.
settings.handbookProvidersIntro: The app renders inside a stack of providers whose nesting order is load-bearing: who you are sits above which server you are on, which sits above the library, which sits above the plugins, which sit above playback. Each layer can read everything above it and nothing below.
settings.handbookProvidersWhy: That is why a connect or disconnect rebuilds the library instead of blending two, and why a plugin’s provider may call <c>{{hook}}</c> - the pyramid put the library above it on purpose.
settings.handbookSearchFactOperators: Operators narrow it: <c>{{artist}}</c>, <c>{{album}}</c>, <c>{{genre}}</c> - stackable with free text.
settings.handbookSearchFactPlugins: Plugins can answer too: a pasted store link becomes an import command right in the results.
settings.handbookSearchIntro: One search, summoned from anywhere, over songs, artists, albums and lyrics at once. It forgives typos rather than returning nothing, and it remembers what you reached for last time.
settings.handbookServersFactDot: The header’s network dot glances the connection; Manage lands on the Servers pane.
settings.handbookServersIntro: An account can know several servers, but a device is signed into one at a time - the Servers pane is where you move. A mirror can carry the songs you actually listen to, so a small box in the cloud covers for the big one at home when you are away.
settings.handbookStackFactOta: An OTA update is exactly two self-contained files: app.js and app.css.
settings.handbookStackFactServer: The server owns the heavy work: imports, effects, the discover feed, enrichment.
settings.handbookStackIntro: One TypeScript + React app, built with Vite, is the whole frontend - the phone, the desktop and the browser all run the same bundle inside Tauri shells or a plain tab. The hub is a Rust server; identity is a separate registry service the devices and servers both trust.
settings.handbookSuggestionsDiscover: Everything the machine picks for you sits on Discover, its own tab beside the Library. The mixes are built on the server from your listening and contain only music you already own, so they play the instant you tap them; Music Date is the deck of things the collector went and fetched on your behalf, waiting on a listen to earn a place; the charts it keeps, the lists it suggests and the shelves it reads from your history are all there too.
settings.handbookSuggestionsFactPerListener: Suggestions are per listener: two people on one server get different shelves.
settings.handbookSuggestionsFactPlays: A card you do not own yet still plays: tapping it opens Now Playing downloading.
settings.handbookSuggestionsLibrary: The Library is only what you saved or made: your liked songs, your playlists, the music you added. Looking for one song you do not own yet is still a search - the search field takes a Discover scope, which looks outward instead of at your shelves.
settings.handbookUpdatesFactAbout: About shows every check’s outcome - silence is the one thing an updater must never be.
settings.handbookUpdatesFactRefused: A bundle needing a newer native shell than yours is refused, not half-applied.
settings.handbookUpdatesIntro: The app checks for a new frontend shortly after launch and every few hours after, downloads it in the background, verifies it, and offers a restart with a banner that says what changed. No store, no cable - a TypeScript fix reaches every device the same day it ships.
settings.hapticsGloss: Ticks from the Taptic Engine as you tap, play, and spin the disc.
settings.hapticsHint: Ticks from the Taptic Engine as you tap, play, and spin the disc. Only things you actually press answer - scrolling and loading stay silent.
settings.headerLyricsHint: How the song's words are spelled across the artwork behind the header, when the track has synced lyrics. Random draws a new one each song.
settings.importServerGloss: Which server fetches imported links, before the songs are copied across to your library.
settings.keepPlaceGloss: Sends what you are playing and how far in to your AttackFM account.
settings.languageFooter: Arabic lays the whole app out right-to-left.
settings.modelEndpointGloss: Where the server sends its AI requests - an Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible origin.
settings.notifyDeviceHint: Where the app's news is put, and how much of it there is. Both are about this phone rather than your account, so another device can answer differently.
settings.notifyDiscoveryHint: New music picked for your taste, and songs the collector has queued up for a date.
settings.notifyKindsHint: Only a few things are worth interrupting somebody for. Each one switches off on its own, and it switches off for every device you have at once.
settings.notifyNoDevices: No device is registered yet, so nothing can arrive however these are set.
settings.notifyOnDeviceGloss: Puts the app's news in your phone's notification tray, so it reaches you without the app open.
settings.notifyOsHint: Puts the same news in the notification tray, so it reaches you without the app open. Skipped while you are already looking at the app.
settings.notifyRefused: Your device is refusing notifications from AttackFM. Turn them back on for this app in the system settings.
settings.notifyRefusedFlip: Your device is refusing notifications from AttackFM. Turn them back on for this app in the system settings, then flip this again.
settings.notifySignedOutBody: Sign in and the switches appear — each kind is a per-account choice the server honours for every device at once.
settings.notifyTestGloss: Puts one notification in the tray now, to check they arrive.
settings.notifyTestHint: Puts one in the tray now, so you can see what arriving looks like before you rely on it.
settings.notifyTestUnsupported: This build cannot reach the notification tray. Desktop and older installs need a fresh version of the app itself, not just an update.
settings.notifyVerboseGloss: Ring for background work too: downloads starting, songs being pulled into stems, the AI running.
settings.notifyVerboseHint: Downloads starting, songs being pulled into stems, and the AI's background passes starting and finishing.
settings.onlineLookupsGloss: Lyrics from LRCLIB and album art from Apple, keyed by track titles.
settings.pluginBooksDescription: Your audiobook shelf — read your books and pick up where you left off.
settings.pluginBooksDetails: The reading side of audiobooks, built in: your shelf of books, however they got into the library, played back with chapters and your place kept across devices. It shows as a Music/Books toggle at the top of the Library; turn it off and that toggle goes away. Getting books IN is a separate job — the Audible downloader does it for books you own, and anything dropped in the library’s Audiobooks folder is shelved here too.
settings.pluginBuyDescription: Find where to buy a song or album as an MP3 or FLAC download.
settings.pluginBuyDetails: Adds a Buy option wherever the app offers to add music - Discover cards, search results, an artist’s catalogue. Choosing it opens a sheet of stores (Bandcamp, Qobuz, 7digital, HDtracks, the iTunes Store, Amazon Music), each searched for the song or album, so you can buy it as an MP3 or a lossless FLAC and own the file. Ships on: when no downloader is enabled, Buy is how you still get the track.
settings.pluginVisualizersDescription: Thirteen audio-reactive visualizers - vector scopes, fractals, particles - where the CD spins.
settings.pluginVisualizersDetails: Pick Visualizer under Now Playing’s Artwork style menu and the art square becomes a picture of the sound: a spectrum halo, a vector scope, Lissajous curves, a particle nebula, a Julia set, the demoscene plasma, a noise flow field, a kaleidoscope, a starfield warp, a spiral galaxy, the Lorenz butterfly, beat-dropped ripples and a rose curve. Every one is painted in the record’s own accent colour and moves to the live audio. Tap the picture to cycle through them, or choose one here.
settings.saveHistoryGloss: Reports finished listens to your server, which feeds recently-played and your mixes.
settings.shakeFlickGloss: Shake to change shuffle, flick left or right to change songs, on Now Playing.
settings.shakeFlickHint: On the Now Playing screen: shake to change shuffle, flick left or right to move between songs. Off by default because a gesture that misreads costs you the song you were listening to — walking, running and a pocket are all ignored, but a phone that lives in a bag may still find a way.
settings.shareListeningGloss: Friends on your server can open your full profile; friends elsewhere see your week.
settings.sizeFooter: Scales the whole interface — text, artwork, controls and spacing alike.
settings.sleepTimerGloss: Fades out and pauses when the time is up.
settings.spacingFooter: How tightly things pack together, at whatever size you have chosen.
settings.stemPrefetchGloss: Pulls liked and playlisted songs apart in the background so the Pads open instantly.
settings.streamingQualityGloss: Lossless sends the original file; Data saver re-encodes to a bitrate you pick.
settings.summaryDownloadsIdle: The queue, and anything that stalled
settings.summaryHandbook_one: How it all works, in {{count}} page
settings.summaryHandbook_other: How it all works, in {{count}} pages
settings.summaryLocalAi: Ask for things, your moods, the model, and what it has been doing
settings.summaryNotifications: What the app may interrupt you for
settings.title: Settings
settings.updateStaged: v{{version}} is ready — restart to apply
settings.videoClipsGloss: The song's short looping clip behind the full player.
settings.videoClipsHint: Plays the song's short looping clip behind the full player. Each new song pulls down a few megabytes of video, and your server asks Spotify for it by song title. Off leaves the blurred cover.
settings.whereYouListenBody: Servers saved to your AttackFM account, wherever you sign in. Switch between them, or hand someone a way into yours.
settings.wifiOnlyGloss: Automatic downloads wait for Wi-Fi; playing, pins and Check now are unaffected.

visualizers.artLabel: Visualizer: {{name}}. Tap for the next one.
visualizers.flowNote: Streamlines through a drifting noise field.
visualizers.footnote: Choose Visualizer under Now Playing’s Artwork style menu (long-press the art) to show it. Drawn on the device from the live audio - nothing leaves the phone.
visualizers.galaxyNote: Spiral arms, lit band by band.
visualizers.haloNote: Spectrum bars around a breathing ring.
visualizers.juliaNote: A Julia set whose seed orbits with the music.
visualizers.kaleidoNote: One spectrum wedge, mirrored eight ways.
visualizers.lissajousNote: X-Y curves whose ratio the bands bend.
visualizers.lorenzNote: The butterfly attractor, stirred by the music.
visualizers.nebulaNote: Particles burst on the beat and drift in the glow.
visualizers.paneDescription: Thirteen ways to draw the sound, in the spot where the CD spins. Pick one here, or tap the picture while it plays to cycle through them. Every one paints in the record’s own accent colour.
visualizers.plasmaNote: The old demoscene plasma, breathing with the bass.
visualizers.ripplesNote: Rings dropped on every beat, crossing as they grow.
visualizers.roseNote: A rose curve whose petals follow the treble.
visualizers.scopeNote: A vector oscilloscope ring, drawn from the spectrum.
visualizers.warpNote: A starfield that throws itself at you on the beat.
